title: Rounds 48-49 stopped: the deeper search was too slow
text: With 128 simulations per move, a Mini-AlphaZero move took about 0.37 s at full speed, and the ranking rounds ran at low priority on a fully loaded machine (both finalists' training, the podcast narration and another project's job). After an hour rounds 48 and 49 had still not finished, so I stopped them; their games are lost. Three fixes: (1) the PUCT selection in the tree search was numpy on 3-element arrays, about 10,000 calls per move; it's now compiled with numba and checked to give identical choices on 20,000 random nodes; a move now takes 0.23 s. (2) In matches, Mini-AlphaZero keeps the subtree of the position that actually happened, so earlier simulations count toward the 128 (same depth, less work). (3) In the duel, ranking rounds run at normal priority, taking an even share from both trainers. The supervisor also never starts a round while another one runs. Ranking resumes with round 50.

title: Do they learn to trap each other? Partly.
text: Measured from the ranking replays (model-vs-model games). Nearly every game is decided by separation: the bikes end up walled off from each other and the bigger side wins 94% of the time (round 46). The top two win that split: when Mini-AlphaZero separates from an opponent it has 67% of the free space on average and wins by more than 20 points 76% of the time (63% in round 8); PPO 64% and 65% (49% in round 8). NEAT and DQN lose most splits. Games got longer (median 139 ticks in round 1, 245 now) and the loser wastes fewer cells (52 -> 28). But nobody traps early on purpose: separations come around tick 155-165, and the territory bot, which cuts early (tick 93), now ends up with only 39% of the space against the models. Likely reasons: Mini-AlphaZero's 32-simulation search sees only 2-3 simultaneous moves ahead, the learners are only paid at the end of a game, and the models see a 15x15 window, not the whole board.

title: Change: PPO's learning rate 3e-4 -> 1e-4
text: All four models have been flat for about 12 hours (rounds 23-46), measured against the fixed territory bot: PPO 90-100%, Mini-AlphaZero 50-75%, NEAT and DQN bouncing between 10% and 80% with no trend. It's rock-paper-scissors at the top: Mini-AlphaZero beats PPO 70-90% head to head, PPO beats the territory bot more often. With about 18 hours of training left, one low-risk change: PPO's learning rate drops to a third, the classic way to fine-tune past a plateau. DQN is left alone because every restart empties its replay memory; nothing obvious would help NEAT. Success = PPO winning more against Mini-AlphaZero within 3-4 rounds.

title: Speed bug after the knockout: 2 cores made PPO and DQN slower
text: After 12:01 every model got 2 cores, and PPO and DQN told torch to use 2 threads. On networks this small the threads mostly wait for each other: a benchmark gave 39 ms per DQN step with 1 torch thread and 126 ms with 2. DQN had dropped from about 1,150 to 676 moves per second, PPO from about 3,900 to 2,700, for 40 minutes. Fixed at 12:41: torch always uses 1 thread, and the second core speeds up the observation code (numba, parallel over games). NEAT and Mini-AlphaZero were not affected: they use 2 worker processes.

title: Caught before the knockout: two multi-core bugs
text: After the first knockout every model gets 2 cores, which switches NEAT and Mini-AlphaZero to a pool of worker processes for the first time. title: Change 2 for CMA-ES: restart its search

title: Rating scale: a stronger yardstick from round 8
text: Round 7 (01:32): Mini-AlphaZero 2246, PPO 2178, NEAT 1935, DQN 1846, CMA-ES 1662. The big jumps (+290, +247) are mostly an artifact: the top four beat the pinned space-filler bot 20/20, so the scale had nothing to hold it and drifted upwards. The order between the models is unaffected (they play each other 20 games per pair), so the knockouts and the catch-up rule are unaffected too. From round 8 a fourth fixed bot plays: the territory bot (the move that claims the most cells before the opponent; it beats space-filler 39/40). It's rated on the current scale in round 8 and pinned at that value from then on.

title: Change: CMA-ES now practises against the other contestants
text: After five rounds stuck around 1600 (the others are at 1830-1910), CMA-ES's opponents change from bots + its own past champions to mostly the newest ranking-round checkpoints of PPO, DQN and NEAT. Its weights, search distribution and step size are kept; only who it plays changes. Expectation: its fitness drops at first (harder opponents), and its rating should rise within 2-4 rounds if the method can learn from them. The first knockout is Thursday 12:00, so this is its chance.

title: Rounds 2-3: PPO leads, DQN's comeback, CMA-ES falls
text: Round 3 (23:32): PPO 1896, NEAT 1871, Mini-AlphaZero 1820, DQN 1715, CMA-ES 1561. DQN gained 375 points in round 2, right after its random-exploration schedule reached its floor (3% at 1.5 M steps). CMA-ES went from first to last: it trains only against the bots and its own past champions, which no longer push it (best fitness has flattened out around 1.0 out of a possible 1.05). Not broken and still slowly improving, so no change yet; if it keeps falling over the next rounds, the planned change is to add other contestants' checkpoints to its opponents.

title: Restart after a bug in the supervisor
text: In the first few minutes the supervisor couldn't see its own trainers (its process pattern started with '-m', which the pgrep tool reads as an option), so every 20 seconds it started another copy of all five. After 3 minutes about 50 trainers were fighting over 8 cores and the same files. Fixed (the pattern is anchored on the full interpreter path, and the supervisor now refuses to run two trainers for one model), all runs were wiped, and the tournament restarted from scratch at 22:07.

title: Training has started
text: All five trainers passed a 2-minute smoke test (PPO ~2,000 steps/s, DQN ~1,000 steps/s, NEAT ~15 s per generation of 120, CMA-ES ~4 s per generation of 32, Mini-AlphaZero ~1,200 self-play games per hour, each on one core). A test ranking round with 2-minute-old models already put the tree-search model level with the space-filler bot: search with a perfect model of the game is a big head start. Each model now gets one pinned core (cores 0-4); cores 5-7 run ranking rounds and this website.

title: The tournament is being built
text: Wednesday evening: the Tron simulator (30x30 board, numba) and this website go up first so you can follow along. Next: the five trainers (PPO, DQN, NEAT, CMA-ES, Mini-AlphaZero), the ranking rounds and the supervisor that runs the catch-up rule and the knockouts. Training starts as soon as every model passes a 5-minute sanity test.
